Here's something most event briefs never mention:

The hardest part of producing a 400-person international incentive trip isn't the program.
It's the 11 weeks of invisible decisions before anyone boards a plane.

Vendor vetting across 3 countries.
Contingency budgets built into contingency budgets.
A technical rider translated, localized, and rehearsed with a crew that speaks a different production language than you do.

After 1,500+ events in 130+ destinations, the pattern is consistent:
The experiences that land hardest with senior audiences are the ones where every friction point was quietly removed before it existed.

HR and marketing leaders who've run large-scale corporate events — what's the operational variable that surprised you most the first time you did it at scale?

Happy to share how we approach it. DM open.

facebook.text:
Most people see the gala dinner.
They don't see the 11 weeks before it.

Logistics scouted across 3 continents. Venue contracts negotiated in 2 languages. A 47-point technical rider sent to a local crew that had never run an international production.

By the time guests walked in, every decision had already been made — twice.

That's what 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations teaches you: the experience guests remember is built entirely on the work they never notice.

What's the part of your next event that keeps you up at night? Drop it in the comments — we've probably solved it before. 👇
